hero.title: OptionPricing
hero.subtitle: An Object-Oriented Web Platform for Interactive Option Valuation and Greeks Analysis
hero.tagline: Price options with Black-Scholes, a binomial tree, or Monte Carlo behind one price() and greeks() interface. The pyoptionpricing Python package powers a FastAPI backend and a Next.js dashboard.
hero.impact: Built for the Object-Oriented Programming II course in the Master of Quantitative Finance at Rutgers University. The same call prices European, American, Asian, and barrier options, and implied volatility works with any model. The volatility surface uses synthetic prices, not live market data.

problems.d: Black-Scholes, a tree, and a simulation each have their own code. A caller should price any of them with price() and greeks() and not care which.
American options need a tree that checks exercise at every node. Asian and barrier payoffs depend on the whole path, so they need simulated paths.

Implied volatility has to work with any model, not only Black-Scholes. The solver calls each option's own price() inside Brent's method and raises a clear error when the market price is out of bounds.
Prices are checked against known results: put-call parity, tree convergence to Black-Scholes, Monte Carlo within standard error, and Greeks against finite differences.

layers.title: Option hierarchy

layers.title: OptionFactory + PricingEngine
layers.desc: The factory builds the right class from model, style, and type. The engine prices any Option the same way

layers.title: FastAPI
layers.desc: Eight POST endpoints plus /models and /health. Pydantic validation, 422 on bad input, no model logic in the routes

layers.title: Next.js dashboard
layers.desc: One form, price and Greeks cards, and Recharts views for compare, payoff, convergence, paths, and the IV smile

highlights: Black-Scholes with analytical delta, gamma, theta, vega, and rho
CRR binomial tree for European and American options
Monte Carlo with standard error, plus Asian and barrier options
Implied volatility with Brent's method, for any model, plus a smile across strikes and maturities
Side-by-side model comparison and a binomial convergence chart
Library on PyPI: pip install pyoptionpricing
